mcpTools.name: ha_history_get_current_time
mcpTools.description:
Returns the current date and time from the Home Assistant server (Oslo).
Call this before making any time-based query when the user uses a relative or named time
expression: "last month", "this winter", "yesterday", "last year", "in april", "recently".
Do not rely on your training data to infer the current date — it will often be wrong.
Skip only if an absolute ISO date range has already been stated in this conversation.

mcpTools.name: ha_history_list_entities
mcpTools.description:
Lists Oslo sensors that have historical data available.
Each result includes the entity_id, friendly name, room/area, unit, and sensor type.
Call this to find the correct entity_id before querying any sensor you don't already know.
Skip only if the entity_id was already resolved earlier in this conversation.
Also use for explicit sensor discovery or when a previous call returned an ambiguous match.
Binary sensors (motion, doors, presence) require domain="binary_sensor" — they have no
statistics so they won't appear in a plain search without specifying that domain.

domain.description: Filter by entity domain prefix. Use "sensor" for numeric/measurement sensors (temperature, energy, power). Use "binary_sensor" for on/off sensors (motion, doors, windows). Leave empty to include all domains.

search.description: Search term matched against entity_id, friendly name, device name, and area name. E.g. "temperature", "bedroom", "energy", "door", "salon", "kitchen".

mcpTools.name: ha_history_get_sensor_stats
mcpTools.description:
Computes statistics for a Oslo sensor measuring instantaneous values:
temperature, humidity, CO₂, pressure, illuminance, or power draw in Watts.
Use for: "What was the lowest temperature last night?", "Average humidity in April?",
"Warmest day last summer?", "How many days above 25°C?", "Which days had frost?",
"At what time of day is it usually hottest?", "Which day of the week is most humid?"
Do NOT use for energy consumption (kWh) → use ha_history_get_consumption.
Do NOT use for event counting → use ha_history_detect_sessions.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (e.g. "sensor.ruuvitag_fc8f_temperature"). Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

aggregation.description:
"mean": average. "min": lowest. "max": highest. "median": middle value.
"count" (requires group_by + filter): counts per slot how many readings satisfied
  the filter condition. Returns "N/M" per slot — e.g. "18/30 days at 06:00 exceeded 21°C".
  Use for: "how many days at each hour exceeded 25°C?",
           "how many weeks on each day-of-week was humidity above 70%?"
Choose: "hottest" → "max", "coldest" → "min", "average/typical" → "mean",
"how many X had Y?" with group_by → "count".

interval.description:
"none": one value for the whole period (default).
"hour"/"day"/"week"/"month": time series — one value per bucket.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.
Cannot be used together with group_by.

group_by.description:
Groups all readings by a repeating time unit across the full period, then applies
the aggregation. Ideal for pattern questions:
"hour_of_day": 24 buckets (00:00–23:00) — "at what time of day is it usually hottest?"
"day_of_week": 7 buckets (Mon–Sun) — "which day of the week is most humid?"
Cannot be used with interval. filter_operator/filter_value work normally on top.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where the aggregated value satisfies [op] filter_value.
Requires interval (not "none") or group_by. Response includes matching bucket count.
E.g. frost days: aggregation="min", filter_operator="<", filter_value=0

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval time-series only (not scalar or group_by). Default: 100. Pass "all" for the complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

mcpTools.name: ha_history_get_consumption
mcpTools.description:
Calculates how much energy, water, gas, or other resource was consumed or produced
in Oslo over a time period.
Use for: "How much electricity did the car charger use in February?",
"Total electricity last month?", "Solar production last week?",
"Daily energy usage last week", "Compare grid import this April vs last April",
"Which days used more than 10 kWh?"
Always returns consumption (the change over the period), never raw meter readings.
Do NOT use for instantaneous sensors (temperature, power in Watts) → use ha_history_get_sensor_stats.

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities (look for type="cumulative"). E.g. "sensor.electricity_meter_kwh". Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

interval.description:
"none": total consumption for the whole period (default).
"day": daily breakdown. "week": weekly. "month": monthly.
Required when using filter_operator/filter_value.

filter_operator.description:
Filter results to buckets where consumption satisfies [op] filter_value. Requires interval.
E.g. "which days used more than 10 kWh?" → interval="day", filter_operator=">", filter_value=10

filter_value.description: Threshold for filter_operator. Required when filter_operator is set.

max_results.description: Applies to interval breakdown only (not scalar). Default: 100. Pass "all" for complete series. Response shows total count when capped.

comparison.description:
Only applicable with interval="none". Compares the total to a reference period.
"previous_period": equal-length period immediately before.
"same_period_last_year": same calendar dates 1 year ago.
Returns both totals and the absolute/percentage difference.

mcpTools.name: ha_history_detect_sessions
mcpTools.description:
Detects and counts discrete events or activity sessions from Oslo sensor history.
Use for: "How many times was the car charged in February?",
"How many times did the washing machine run last week?",
"How many times was the front door opened?",
"Was there any motion in the garage overnight?",
"What was the longest charging session last month?",
"What time did the last person go to bed each night this week?" (use group_by="day")
For numeric sensors (power in W): uses long-term hourly statistics — full date range.
For binary sensors (motion, door): uses state history — limited to ~10 days.
Returns: event count, total duration, compact session list, or daily summary (with group_by="day").

entity.description: Exact entity_id from ha_history_list_entities. Do not guess.

start_time.description: Period start. Formats: relative (7d/30d/24h/2w/1y), named ("last month"/"last week"/"yesterday"/"last summer"/"Q1"), or ISO ("2026-04-01"). Default: 30d. Special: "overnight" = 22:00 yesterday → 06:00 today.

end_time.description: Period end, same formats as start_time. Default: now.

threshold.description:
For numeric/power sensors only: minimum value to count as "active".
Example: 100 for Watts (heater or EV charger). Omit for binary sensors.
Required for numeric sensors — without it the tool treats the sensor as binary.

min_duration_minutes.description:
Minimum session duration in minutes. Filters out sessions shorter than this. Default: 1.
Note: for numeric sensors using hourly statistics, the minimum meaningful
value is 60 min (one hour bucket). Values below 60 have no additional effect.

max_gap_minutes.description:
Maximum inactivity gap to bridge between two active periods, treating them as
one session. Default: 0 (no merging). Useful for devices with scheduled pauses:
e.g. washing machine with a 1–2h break between cycles (set 90–150).
Note: for numeric sensors with hourly statistics, gaps are in whole hours —
values below 60 have no effect; use multiples of 60 (e.g. 90, 120).

group_by.description:
Group sessions by calendar day. Returns one compact row per day:
  date | session count | first session start | last session end | total active
Use for high-frequency sensors (motion, door) where the session list is too long,
or when daily patterns matter: "when did activity start each morning?",
"how many times per day did the washing machine run?"
For cross-midnight patterns (bedtime, night shifts), combine with day_start_hour=6.
Summary stats (total sessions, active days, avg/day) always cover the full dataset.

day_start_hour.description:
Only with group_by="day". Shifts the day boundary from midnight to a later hour (0–23).
Default: 0 (midnight). Set to 6 for "night" grouping: a day runs 06:00 → next 05:59,
so post-midnight activity (e.g. 01:30) is attributed to the previous evening's date.
Use for: "what time did the last person go to bed each night?",
overnight patterns, night shifts, anything spanning midnight.

max_results.description:
Max rows to return. Default: 20. Pass "all" to list all.
Without group_by: caps individual sessions.
With group_by="day": caps calendar days shown.
Summary stats always cover the full dataset regardless.

comparison.description:
Compare session count and duration to a reference period.
"previous_period": the immediately preceding equal-length period.
"same_period_last_year": the same calendar period 12 months ago.
